properties.areaDesc: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 21 at 7:14PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
CORRECTED HEADLINE.

...HEAVY SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS YAP STATE AND PALAU
THROUGH MIDWEEK...
...WEST WINDS TO BE GUSTY AT TIMES...

An active monsoon pattern has developed across Western Micronesia
with recent satellite imagery showing broad areas of heavy showers
and thunderstorms. Midday satellite-derived surface wind data depicts
15 to 20 mph west winds across Western Yap State and Palau.

Computer models point to a continuation of these conditions into
midweek with periods of heavy showers moving across the islands,
occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts and choppy seas. Both
Yap and Palau are in the monsoon inflow of JTWC's Invest 91W, (that
is located near 11N144E between Yap and Guam). As 91W continues to
organize showers are expected to remain widespread and heavy at
times. Model guidance suggest up to 1 to 2 inches of rain a day
through Wednesday, then tapering down to about 0.5 inch for the
following few days.

Residents should continue to monitor forecasts and listen for any
marine advisories that may be issued over the next several days. Be
aware of the latest weather conditions and trends before traveling
between islands. Stay up-to-date with all the latest forecasts at
weather.gov/gum and by following the latest information from your
local Weather Service Office.

Suffolk, Southern Queens and Southern Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Life-threatening rip currents are likely for all
people entering the surf zone. Anyone visiting the beaches
should stay out of the surf. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

into late week.

a direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face
the shore and yell or wave for help.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Central Athens County in southeastern Ohio...
Southwestern Morgan County in southeastern Ohio...
Northeastern Vinton County in southeastern Ohio...
West Central Washington County in southeastern Ohio...

* WHEN...Until 1045 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying

warned area.

deaths occur in vehicles.

800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 21 at 4:21AM EDT until September 26 at 12:00PM EDT by NWS Northern Indiana
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Indiana...

Wabash River near Bluffton IN affecting Wells County.

Wabash River near Linn Grove affecting Adams and Wells Counties.

For the Wabash River...including Linn Grove, Bluffton IN...Minor
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Wabash River near Linn Grove.

* WHEN...Until Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, Secondary roads are blocked. Roads near the
east side of Geneva begin to flood. Some evacuations may be
required and property needs to be transferred to higher ground.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:45 AM EDT Monday the stage was 13.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:45 AM EDT Monday was 14.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Friday afternoon and continue falling to 9.7 feet early Saturday
morning.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Detailed river forecasts and additional information can be found at
www.weather.gov/iwx under Rivers and Lakes.

This statement will be updated within the next 12 to 24 hours.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 21 at 4:11AM EDT until September 25 at 3:12PM EDT by NWS Northern Indiana
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Indiana...Ohio...

Saint Marys River at St. Mary's River near Fort Wayne affecting
Allen IN County.

Saint Marys River near Decatur affecting Van Wert, Allen IN and
Adams Counties.

For the Saint Marys River...including Decatur, St. Mary's River near
Fort Wayne...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Saint Marys River at St. Mary's River near Fort Wayne.

* WHEN...Until Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Some residents in the Winchester Road area
may need to be evacuated. Property damage begins in some areas at
this level.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:45 AM EDT Monday the stage was 16.2 feet and rising.
- Bankfull stage is 14.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 16.6 feet
just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
Thursday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Detailed river forecasts and additional information can be found at
www.weather.gov/iwx under Rivers and Lakes.

This statement will be updated within the next 12 to 24 hours.

properties.areaDesc: Delaware Beaches; Eastern Monmouth; Atlantic Coastal Cape May; Coastal Atlantic; Coastal Ocean
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued September 21 at 4:10AM EDT until September 22 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Delaware and New Jersey coasts.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Always obey posted Beach Flags. If you enter the surf zone,
always have a floatation device with you. Don't go into the water
at unguarded beaches. If caught in a rip current, relax and float
and do not swim against the current. If able, swim parallel to
the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or
wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 21 at 1:02AM MDT until September 23 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, north central,
northeast, southeast, and west central New Mexico, including the
following areas, in central New Mexico, Central Highlands, Eastern
Lincoln County, Estancia Valley, Lower Rio Grande Valley, Middle
Rio Grande Valley including the Albuquerque Metro Area, San Agustin
Plains and Adjacent Lowlands, Sandia and Manzano Mountains
including Edgewood, South Central Highlands, South Central
Mountains and Upper Tularosa Valley. In east central New Mexico, De
Baca County and Guadalupe County. In north central New Mexico, East
Slopes Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Espanola Valley, Glorieta Mesa
Including Glorieta Pass, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands,
Santa Fe Metro Area and Southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains. In
northeast New Mexico, Eastern San Miguel County, Far Northeast
Highlands, Harding County and Northeast Highlands. In southeast New
Mexico, Chaves County Plains and Southwest Chaves County. In west
central New Mexico, Southwest Mountains, West Central Highlands and
West Central Mountains.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.
Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A dangerous surge of monsoon moisture will arrive Tuesday and
Wednesday with widespread heavy rain.  Scattered occurrences of
flash flooding are likely, and there will probably be some main
stem river and tributary flooding, as the most likely rain amount
by Wednesday afternoon exceeds 2 inches in many locations along
and east of the central mountain chain, and 1 inch in many
locations westward to the continental divide. Stronger storms
will produce torrential rainfall at rates over 2 inches per hour,
and storms will train repeatedly in succession over some
locations, with locally heavier rain amounts reaching 4 to 6
inches over portions of central and eastern New Mexico.  Heavy
rain will likely continue Wednesday night over eastern areas,
then showers and storms with locally heavy rainfall are forecast
to return along and east of the continental divide again on
Thursday.
- Rapid runoff and flash flooding will be most likely in complex
terrain, below recent burn scars, low-lying areas, urban areas,
normally dry arroyos, and near rivers and streams.  As the event
unfolds, locations with saturated ground will also become prone
to rapid runoff and flash flooding from additional rounds of
storms.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.  Never drive through flood
waters.  Most flash flood deaths occur in automobiles.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 21 at 4:49PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
An active monsoon pattern has developed across Western Micronesia
with recent satellite imagery showing broad areas of heavy showers
and thunderstorms. Midday satellite-derived surface wind data depicts
15 to 20 mph west winds across Western Yap State and Palau.

Computer models point to a continuation of these conditions into
midweek with periods of heavy showers moving across the islands,
occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts and choppy seas. Both
Yap and Palau are in the monsoon inflow of JTWC's Invest 91W, (that
is located near 11N144E between Yap and Guam). As 91W continues to
organize showers are expected to remain widespread and heavy at
times. Model guidance suggest up to 1 to 2 inches of rain a day
through Wednesday, then tapering down to about 0.5 inch for the
following few days.

Residents should continue to monitor forecasts and listen for any
marine advisories that may be issued over the next several days. Be
aware of the latest weather conditions and trends before traveling
between islands. Stay up-to-date with all the latest forecasts at
weather.gov/gum and by following the latest information from your
local Weather Service Office.

properties.description:
* WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...All of Puerto Rico, including Vieques and Culebra, and the
U.S. Virgin Islands.


* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 3 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to
heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest
across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.
properties.instruction:

the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.senderName: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 20 at 11:18PM MDT until September 23 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Much of south-central New Mexico and Far West Texas,
including El Paso, Las Cruces, and the Mesilla Valley.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of arroyos,
rivers, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded, resulting in road closures.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An early season back door cold front will interact with a late
season plume of deep monsoonal moisture, bringing several rounds
of thunderstorms with torrential downpours to the region Tuesday
afternoon through Wednesday evening. Repeated thunderstorms may
tend to focus in one or two areas, resulting in higher end
precipitation totals. The most critical period with the heaviest
rain potential will likely be Tuesday night into Wednesday
morning.
- A broad swath of moderate to locally heavy rainfall is likely to
affect most of the Watch area between late Tuesday afternoon and
Wednesday evening, with typical, scattered monsoon season flood
impacts. However, there is increasing potential for a narrow band
of repeated thunderstorms which will result in particularly heavy
rainfall amounts, possibly exceeding 3 inches in a 6 to 12 hour
period, resulting in higher-end impacts. Forecast models
currently favor placing the focus for heaviest rainfall over the
Mesilla Valley and El Paso. But forecasts this far out,
especially when dealing with thunderstorms, are simply not
accurate enough to precisely tell yet where exactly this area of
heaviest rainfall will set up. It could just as easily shift west
or east and avoid the more populated corridor.
- http://www.weather.gov/ElPaso
properties.instruction:
The forecast will be fine-tuned and will evolve over time. You should
monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood Warnings
Tuesday afternoon and evening. The Wednesday morning commute may also

levels to rise.
